questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039122/assets/c42f5aac98d31b7a66a60eebae34b5e83cb62f3ba4801595a81dd9bb57706384.png)

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(0,0),$ and passes through the point $(4,-8).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=2pt,\,y=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(4,-8),$ we can substitute $x=4$ and $y=-8$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}4=2pt \\ -8=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2pt \\ 2 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{2}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-8 & =p{(\frac{2}{p})}^{2} \\ -8 & =p\cdot \frac{4}{{p}^{2}} \\ -8 & =\frac{4}{p} \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=2(-\frac{1}{2})t,\,y=(-\frac{1}{2}){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=-t,\,y=-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}.
$$

questions.problem: Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ and which passes through the point $(-7,-7)?$
questions.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical parabola  that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=2pt,\,y=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(-7,-7),$ we can substitute $x=-7$ and $y=-7$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}-7=2pt \\ -7=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-7 & =2pt \\ t & =-\frac{7}{2p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-7 & =p{(-\frac{7}{2p})}^{2} \\ -7 & =p\cdot \frac{49}{4{p}^{2}} \\ -7 & =\frac{49}{4p} \\ 4p & =-7 \\ p & =-\frac{7}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=2(-\frac{7}{4})t,\,y=(-\frac{7}{4}){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=-\frac{7}{2}t,\,y=-\frac{7}{4}{t}^{2}.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following parabola:

$$
x=4{t}^{2},\,y=6t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

The Cartesian equation of the parabola is

${y}^{2}=$
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{x}{4},\,t=\frac{y}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{{y}^{2}}{36}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=\frac{x}{4}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{36} & =\frac{x}{4} \\ {y}^{2} & =9x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation of the parabola is ${y}^{2}=9x.$

$$
x=-2{t}^{2},\,y=-4t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).

First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =-\frac{x}{2},\,t=-\frac{y}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{{y}^{2}}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=-\frac{x}{2}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{16} & =-\frac{x}{2} \\ {y}^{2} & =-8x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation of the parabola is ${y}^{2}=-8x.$

where $p$ is constant.
